_note: Generated by scripts/build_landchange.py; regenerate rather than edit.
method: NISAR GCOV backscatter, frequency A (~20 m), every pass on one track/frame per site so images line up. Images: R = HH, G = HV, B = HH/HV (the crop sites' stretches). Change map: HH brightness difference in dB between two dates (half resolution, 5 x 5 smoothed); dB stored as 8-bit -30..5.

sites.name: Kīlauea summit
sites.headline: Lava refills Halemaʻumaʻu crater
sites.story: Dozens of short lava-fountaining episodes in Halemaʻumaʻu crater through 2025-26, each adding lava to the crater floor.
sites.look_for: The crater floor changing as new lava covers it, and tephra to the southwest.

sites.headline: The tour's view of Kīlauea
sites.story: The area the guided tour has you draw, rendered like the gallery's images.
sites.look_for: The caldera and its crater floor.

sites.name: Krasheninnikov volcano
sites.headline: A new lava flow down the south flank
sites.story: Krasheninnikov, quiet for centuries, erupted in 2025-26 and sent lava flows down its flanks.
sites.look_for: A long, bright flow running south from the summit area that isn't there in June.

sources.label: Space.com: Satellite spies an erupting volcano

sites.name: Jakobshavn Isbræ
sites.headline: The ice in the fjord changes from June to October
sites.story: Greenland's fastest glacier, flowing tens of metres a day into an ice-packed fjord.
sites.look_for: The glacier front and the fjord's ice, pass by pass.

sites.name: Jamuna River
sites.headline: Channels and sandbars look different after the monsoon
sites.story: A braided river whose channels and sandbars shift every monsoon.
sites.look_for: Where water (dark) and sand (bright) sit in June and in November.

sites.name: Langtang Lirung slope collapse

event.label: Rock slope failure and debris flow

sites.headline: A streak of change between the passes either side of 26 August
sites.story: On 26 August 2026 a very large rock slope on Langtang Lirung failed and started a debris flow and flood that swept through Nepal and Tibet.
sites.look_for: A streak of strong change between 19 and 31 August, absent from the pairs before and after, starting about half a kilometre from the reported source (28.29°N, 85.53°E) and running northwest down the valley. Consistent with the debris flow; not a mapped outline of it.

sources.label: Eos Landslide Blog: the landslide behind the 26 August debris flow

sites.name: Anak Krakatau
sites.headline: New features on the west coast after the eruption
sites.story: After a late-September 2026 eruption, officials reported two small new formations around the island.
sites.look_for: A new bright feature on the west coast on 30 September. Small for 20 m pixels.

sites.name: Etna

event.label: Lava flow reported toward the Valle del Leone

sites.headline: A ribbon of change where a lava flow was reported
sites.story: On 26 June 2026 a lava flow was reported moving toward the Valle del Leone from a fracture at about 3,000 m.
sites.look_for: A ribbon of change east-northeast of the summit, clearest from 17 June to 27 October.

sites.name: Rio Branco at Caracaraí
sites.headline: Bright streaks appear along the river as the scene darkens
sites.story: An Amazon tributary whose level normally falls through the second half of the year.
sites.look_for: Bright streaks along the channel from June to October, and the whole scene getting darker.

sites.name: Budhi Gandaki landslide
sites.headline: A fresh patch of change at the reported scar
sites.story: On 11 October 2026 a rock slope failed (source area about 500 by 850 m) and ran down the valley as a debris flow.
sites.look_for: A compact patch of change at the scar's reported position, 6 to 18 October.

sites.name: Bang Pakong River floods

event.label: Floods along the Bang Pakong River

sites.headline: Dark patches spread across fields
sites.story: October 2026 rains flooded farmland and fish ponds along the river east of Bangkok.
sites.look_for: Dark patches across the fields, 30 September to 12 October, as standing water would look.
